_doc: Pre-registered detector questions for TypeSafe Jev (POST /v1/systemone). Frozen at the pre-registration commit. {race}, {election}, {candidates} are filled per race by detector/jev.py. The detector never sees AP's call: it reports which candidate (if any) a page says won, and build_state compares that with the confirmed winner afterwards.
model_pin_note: At the freeze, replace jev-latest with the exact version the API reports (e.g. jev-1.13.0) and record it in PREREGISTRATION.md.
election: the United States general election held on 3 November 2026

winner.instructions: According to the text in `page`, who won `race.name` in `race.election`? Answer with a candidate only if the text says that candidate won, was elected, was re-elected, was declared or projected the winner, or that their opponent conceded. Leading, ahead, favored, early returns, partial counts, polls, forecasts and previews are not a win.

criteria_template.candidate: The text says {name} ({party}) won this race in this election.
criteria_template.none: The text does not say that any candidate won this race in this election: it shows leads, partial results, previews, polls or forecasts, or it is about a different election, year, office, state or district.

this_election.instructions: Is the text in `page` about `race.name` in `race.election`? It must be this office in this state (and district, for a House race), in the 3 November 2026 general election. A primary, a runoff held on another day, an earlier year's election, or a different race is not this election.

is_call.instructions: Does the text in `page` report a final outcome of `race.name` in `race.election`: a race call or projection by a news organisation, a concession, or a declared or certified winner? Vote leads, percentages counted so far, and predictions are not a final outcome.

rule._doc: A page NAMES candidate X as the winner when all three hold. Thresholds are validated on detector/testset.jsonl before the freeze.
